description: Athlete's schedule changed — they can only run 4 days instead of 5 going forward. Dean should restructure the plan for 4 days, keep the key sessions (long run, quality), and tell them what to cut.
inbound_sms: My schedule changed and I can only run 4 days a week now. What should I drop?

user.name: Tom
user.experience_level: intermediate — running 4 years, half PR 1:48, first marathon

ground_truth.expected_change: Move from 5 days to 4 days per week. Keep: long run, tempo (quality), and at least 1-2 easy days. Drop: one of the two easy days (Monday or Thursday — either works; Monday is the typical drop since Sunday long run is adjacent). Can consolidate volume from dropped day into remaining easy days slightly.
ground_truth.change_scope: Permanent restructure going forward. Not just this week.
must_include: a specific 4-day structure (which days to run)
which session to drop (recommendation, not just 'you decide')
confirmation that long run and quality work are preserved
must_not_include: dropping the long run to accommodate fewer days
keeping 5 sessions and just shortening them (this doesn't solve the day constraint)
vague advice like 'cut one easy run' without saying which one
ground_truth.tradeoff_to_flag: Weekly volume will drop slightly (~8-10%) — that's acceptable 12 weeks out. Not a big deal to flag, but can mention if natural.
ground_truth.notes: The right call is to drop one easy day (likely Monday given the Sun/Mon adjacency after long run) and keep tempo, intervals, and long run. Dean should give a concrete 4-day structure and explain the rationale briefly. This is a permanent change so next week's plan should reflect it. Keep the answer practical.
